rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is entirely absent, so the first experiment should explore a promising baseline configuration. This experiment tests a multimodal model with scgpt and resnet50 encoders, transformer aggregation, and concat fusion—key components that balance complexity and effectiveness. It clarifies the potential of multimodal approaches with standard encoders, providing foundational insights to guide subsequent exploration.

The existing evidence from config_001 (validation accuracy 0.471) shows that multimodal multiprofile with scgpt and resnet50 performs moderately. This experiment tests replacing the transformer aggregation with avgpool, a simpler method that could improve performance or clarify if transformer's complexity is beneficial. It directly addresses a key design choice (aggregation) with minimal parameter changes, balancing exploration and exploitation while reducing uncertainty about aggregation effectiveness.

The existing evidence shows that avgpool aggregation and concat fusion (config_002) yield higher accuracy than transformer aggregation (config_001). This experiment tests whether replacing the image encoder with a more advanced model (imagenet_vit_l) while maintaining avgpool aggregation and weighted fusion could further improve performance. It directly builds on the previous best configuration by exploring a critical design choice (image encoder) that may significantly impact results.

The existing evidence shows config_019 (scgpt RNA, imagenet_vit_l image, avgpool, weighted) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.542). This experiment tests replacing the RNA encoder with scvi_n200 while keeping the image encoder, aggregation, and fusion method the same. This clarifies whether the RNA encoder choice is critical for performance, a key design decision with high uncertainty. It balances exploitation (building on the best-performing setup) and exploration (testing a new encoder variant).

The existing evidence shows config_026 (0.706 accuracy) is the best so far using scvi_n200 RNA, imagenet_vit_l image, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion. This experiment tests replacing avgpool with transformer aggregation while keeping other components the same, to determine if more complex feature interactions improve accuracy. It directly builds on the strongest current configuration, balancing exploitation of promising components with exploration of aggregation methods.

The existing evidence shows that configurations using scvi_n200 RNA encoder and imagenet_vit_l image encoder (e.g., config_027) achieve high accuracy. This experiment tests whether replacing the RNA encoder with pca_n2000 while keeping the same image encoder, aggregation, and fusion methods could yield similar or better performance. It clarifies the importance of the RNA encoder choice, which remains a key uncertainty. This is the best use of the next experiment to explore a critical design choice with potential for improvement.

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_027) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.7249). This experiment tests scvi_n200 with resnet50 image encoder, transformer aggregation, and concat fusion. It clarifies whether the image encoder (resnet50 vs imagenet_vit_l) or fusion method (concat vs weighted) impacts performance. This is the best use of the remaining budget to explore critical design choices affecting accuracy.

The existing evidence shows config_027 (0.724989 accuracy) is the top performer with scvi_n200 RNA, imagenet_vit_l image, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion. This experiment tests the same RNA and image encoders but with transformer aggregation and concat fusion (vs. weighted fusion in config_027), clarifying whether fusion method impacts performance. It balances exploitation (focusing on top-performing components) and exploration (testing a key design choice variation) under the limited budget.

The existing evidence shows that configurations using scvi_n200 and imagenet_vit_l with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (e.g., config_027) achieve high accuracy. This experiment tests scgpt with imagenet_vit_l, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion, which could clarify if RNA encoder choice (scgpt vs scvi_n200) impacts performance. It is the best use of the final experiment to explore a critical design choice with high potential for improvement.

The existing evidence shows that configurations using scvi_n200 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, and weighted fusion (e.g., config_026, config_027) achieve high accuracy. This experiment tests scvi_n200 RNA with resnet50 image encoder and weighted fusion, which could clarify if the image encoder choice (resnet50 vs. imagenet_vit_l) impacts performance. It is the best use of the final experiment to explore a high-potential parameter combination with a different image encoder.
